=== usage: brunna release 
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: usage: brunna release <project> <tag> [--target <branch|sha>] [--title <title>] [--notes-file <file> | --notes <text>]

=== bad tag: brunna release proj v1..2
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: v1..2 is not a valid tag name (git check-ref-format)

=== nobody at a terminal: brunna release proj v1.0.0
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: nobody is at a terminal to say yes: a release can't be undone, so only your y typed at a terminal publishes one. Run brunna release in your own terminal; nothing was contacted

=== --yes alone: brunna release proj v1.0.0 --yes
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: --yes isn't taken for a release: it can't be undone, so only your y typed at a terminal publishes one. Run brunna release in your own terminal; nothing was contacted

=== in a coding agent's session: brunna release proj v1.0.0
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: brunna release runs only in your own terminal, not in a coding agent's session: a release can't be undone, so the yes has to be yours, typed

=== --target that isn't on the remote: brunna release proj v1.0.0 --target nosuchbranch
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: --target nosuchbranch is neither a branch the remote has nor a commit id

=== unpushed target: brunna release proj v1.0.0 --target <SHA>
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: <SHA> is not a commit on the remote (none of its branches has it): push it first (brunna push), then release; a tag is never made on an unpushed commit

=== plain plan, answered no: brunna release proj v1.0.0
[exit 2]
--- stdout
Release of proj: github.com/o/proj (public)
  tag      v1.0.0 (new: made at the target before the release)
  target   <SHA> (the remote's default branch main)
           add a
           Dev <dev@example.org>, 2026-11-16T10:00:00Z
  commits  2 in all (no earlier tag on the remote)
           <SHA> add a
           <SHA> init
  title    v1.0.0
  notes    none: the release has no notes, and GitHub generates none

!! If Zenodo (or another archive) is connected to this repo, publishing this release makes a permanent archived copy with a DOI that can't be withdrawn (Zenodo's GitHub integration archives every release once it is switched on).

Read so far with your gh login (octo), read-only: the account's name, and that github.com/o/proj has no release named v1.0.0 yet.
To publish it, the platform will use that login on github.com/o/proj to create the tag v1.0.0 at <SHA> and a published release of it. Nothing else of your account is used, and nothing has been changed yet.
Everyone who can see the repo sees the release at once, its watchers are notified, and webhooks and connected services (archives among them) run; deleting it later takes none of that back. So only your typed y goes on, never --yes.
Publish the release with your gh login? [y/N] n
--- stderr
refused: You said no: no release was created, and nothing was changed.

=== published, with notes and an archive file: brunna release proj v1.0.0 --title First release --notes-file <TMP>/notes.md

  commits  3 since v0.9 (<SHA>)
           <SHA> describe the archive
           <SHA> later work
           <SHA> add a
  title    First release
  notes    4 lines:
           > First public release.
           > 
           > - the reader
           > - the writer

--- stderr

=== gh isn't signed in: brunna release proj v1.1.0
[exit 1]
--- stdout
--- stderr
failed: gh isn't signed in to github.com (To get started with GitHub CLI, please run:  gh auth login): sign in with gh auth login and run this again; nothing was changed

=== notes too long to show: brunna release proj v1.4.0 --notes-file <TMP>/long.md
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: the notes are 201 lines and 3 KB: every line is shown before you say yes, so at most 200 lines and 32 KB are taken; shorten them (they can link to a longer changelog)

=== a --target that is also a branch: brunna release proj v1.4.0 --target <SHA>
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: --target <SHA> is a commit id and also a branch on the remote: rename the branch, or name the commit by another length of its id

=== another forge: brunna release proj v1.1.0
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: proj's paths.origin git@gitlab.com:o/proj.git is not a GitHub repo (github.com/<owner>/<repo>): brunna release makes only GitHub releases, with your gh; on another forge, make the release there

=== no remote: brunna release proj v1.1.0
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: proj has no remote (paths.origin): there is nothing to release on

=== not sandboxed: brunna release proj v1.1.0
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: proj is not sandboxed: its sessions can make a release with gh themselves (brunna release is for sandboxed projects, which can't reach gh)

=== not registered: brunna release proj v1.1.0
[exit 2]
--- stdout
--- stderr
refused: proj is not in the registry

=== the project's letter
The release v1.0.0 of github.com/o/proj is published, at <SHA>: https://github.com/o/proj/releases/tag/v1.0.0. Tags and releases are made by the owner (brunna release); there is nothing for you to do.
The release v1.0.0 of github.com/o/proj is published, at <SHA>: https://github.com/o/proj/releases/tag/v1.0.0. Tags and releases are made by the owner (brunna release); there is nothing for you to do.
